# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Build, start the whole app, run the Playwright specs present in e2e/specs, then stop.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

export PORT="${PORT:-3000}"
export BASE_URL="http://localhost:${PORT}"
# Known audit file, shared by the app (bin/start) and the specs (support/audit.ts). Absolute.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

bin/build
bin/start
cleanup() { bin/stop || true; }
trap cleanup EXIT

# Wait for readiness (Actuator health), then run the Playwright specs against BASE_URL.
for i in $(seq 1 60); do
  if curl -fsS "${BASE_URL}/actuator/health" >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep 1
done

# Install deps + the Chromium browser (both cached after first run), then run the specs.
( cd e2e && npm ci --silent && npx --yes playwright install chromium && npx playwright test )
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the Spring Boot app on $PORT (main class net.officefloor.hq.app.Application). On boot, Flyway
# migrates the empty in-memory H2 up to the current schema; Spring serves the SPA (static/) and the
# app's REST endpoints. Returns once
# launching; poll /actuator/health for readiness.
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."
mkdir -p .run

: "${PORT:?PORT must be set}"
JAR="$(ls -t target/*.jar 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || true)"
[ -n "$JAR" ] || { echo "no jar in target/ — run bin/build first" >&2; exit 1; }

# Known audit file (the file-based test-assertion channel). Absolute so app + tests agree.
export AUDIT_FILE="${AUDIT_FILE:-$PWD/.run/audit.log}"

nohup java -jar "$JAR" --server.port="$PORT" --spring.profiles.active=e2e > .run/app.log 2>&1 &
echo $! > .run/app.pid

content.text:
I ran `bin/e2e`. The main "quarterly periods" test passes; the other three tests in the spec fail, and I don't think my change caused any of them.

**What I built**
- **Front end** (`src/main/frontend/features/periods/periods.slot.tsx`): next to the fiscal-year generator there's now a year box (`period-generate-quarters-year`) and a "Generate quarters" button (`period-generate-quarters`). They share the generator's `period-generated` count and `period-generate-error` message. A year that isn't four digits, like "x", is refused on screen.
- **Server**: a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheetId}/periods/generate-quarters`, set up in `generate-quarters.POST.yml`. It checks the user and year (`ValidateQuarterGenerate`), then `SaveQuarterPeriods` adds `<yyyy>-Q1`…`Q4` as Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun, Jul–Sep and Oct–Dec. A quarter is left out if its name is already in use or its dates overlap an existing period. Each new period writes the usual `PERIOD_ADDED` audit line, and the response gives the count. No database change was needed.

In the main test, a period P1 in May means Q2 is skipped, so it makes 3; "x" is refused; running 2026 again makes 0. The audit lines match the spec.

**The three failing tests**
None of them use the quarter generator:
- **Scenarios 1 and 2** expect `sheet-parent` to read literally `__SHEET__-p`. That looks like a placeholder that was never filled in when the spec was generated. A real sheet id can never match it, so these two can't pass without editing the spec, which I'm not allowed to do.
- **Scenario 3** expects Ada's `person-terms` to be blank, but it shows `20`. The step before is a refused attempt to add Ben with terms 20, and that value seems to stay in the person form when Ada is added. That's in the existing people form, not this feature, so I left it alone. I can look into it if you want it fixed.

**Port 3002 was already taken**
An older copy of the app, started at 06:35 today (PID 990954), is still running on port 3002. I didn't start it. With the default port, my build couldn't start and the tests ran against that old copy, so every test failed. I left it running and did the final run on another port with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`. You'll probably want to stop it before running `bin/e2e` normally.
